INVASIVE_DUCTAL_NST.name: Invasive ductal carcinoma / no special type

biomarkers.name: ER (oestrogen receptor)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Positive: endocrine therapy indicated (tamoxifen premenopausal; AI ± OFS postmenopausal/premenopausal as appropriate; SERD elacestrant if ESR1-mut in advanced HR+/HER2- disease). Prognostic (better than ER-neg). ASCO/CAP threshold: ≥1% positive nuclei; 1-10% is reported as ER-low positive

biomarkers.name: PR (progesterone receptor)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Adds prognostic weight beyond ER; ER+/PR- disease is less endocrine-responsive than ER+/PR+

biomarkers.name: HER2 (ERBB2)
biomarkers.prevalence: ~15-20% HER2-positive; HER2-low is common (~45-55% of metastatic breast cancer overall)
biomarkers.clinical_use: HER2+ (IHC 3+ or ISH-amplified): trastuzumab, pertuzumab, T-DM1, T-DXd, tucatinib. HER2-low: T-DXd in unresectable/metastatic disease after prior chemotherapy. HER2-ultralow: T-DXd has shown benefit in HR-positive metastatic disease

biomarkers.name: Ki-67
biomarkers.clinical_use: Prognostic in HR+ disease; used in monarchE trial selection, although current adjuvant abemaciclib use does not require Ki-67 testing in many jurisdictions/guidelines; no universal threshold

biomarkers.name: BRCA1 / BRCA2 (germline)
biomarkers.prevalence: ~5-10% overall; higher in TNBC, young age, family history
biomarkers.clinical_use: PARP inhibitors: olaparib (adjuvant OlympiA in high-risk HER2-negative gBRCA; also metastatic); talazoparib (metastatic). Also implications for risk-reducing surgery and family screening

biomarkers.name: PIK3CA
biomarkers.clinical_use: Alpelisib + fulvestrant in HR+/HER2-/PIK3CA-mut after endocrine progression; inavolisib-based therapy is also supported in this setting

biomarkers.name: ESR1 mutations
biomarkers.prevalence: ~30-40% of ER+/HER2- metastatic disease after AI exposure
biomarkers.clinical_use: Elacestrant (oral SERD) — approved in ESR1-mut ER+/HER2- advanced/metastatic disease after endocrine progression

biomarkers.name: AKT1 / PIK3CA / PTEN alterations
biomarkers.clinical_use: Capivasertib + fulvestrant in HR+/HER2- advanced disease with PI3K/AKT/PTEN pathway alteration (CAPItello-291)

biomarkers.name: MSI / dMMR
biomarkers.clinical_use: Pembrolizumab (tissue-agnostic) if MSI-H/dMMR — rare in breast

biomarkers.name: PD-L1 (SP142 for TNBC IC; CPS 22C3)
biomarkers.prevalence: ~35-45% of metastatic TNBC are PD-L1 positive by CPS ≥10
biomarkers.clinical_use: Pembrolizumab + chemotherapy in metastatic TNBC with CPS ≥10 (22C3, KEYNOTE-355). Atezolizumab with nab-paclitaxel used PD-L1 IC by SP142 in some regions historically; US indication was withdrawn

biomarkers.name: Oncotype DX (21-gene recurrence score)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Chemo benefit prediction in HR+/HER2-/node-negative and selected node-positive disease. In node-negative disease, postmenopausal patients with RS 0-25 generally do not benefit from chemotherapy, whereas chemotherapy is recommended for RS ≥26; interpretation differs by age/menopausal status and nodal status

biomarkers.name: MammaPrint (70-gene assay)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Prognostic genomic assay with MINDACT evidence to help identify clinically high-risk patients who may forgo chemotherapy if genomically low risk

biomarkers.name: CA 15-3, CEA
biomarkers.clinical_use: May assist monitoring in metastatic disease in conjunction with clinical/radiographic assessment; not recommended for routine early-stage surveillance

biomarkers.name: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Useful in advanced disease for noninvasive genotyping and tracking alterations such as ESR1, PIK3CA, and ERBB2; MRD detection after curative-intent therapy remains investigational and is not yet standard of care

biomarkers.name: PALB2 (germline)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Hereditary breast cancer susceptibility gene with therapeutic relevance in metastatic disease; PARP inhibitor sensitivity is supported, although approvals are more limited than for gBRCA

biomarkers.name: NTRK1 / NTRK2 / NTRK3 fusions
biomarkers.prevalence: Very rare in common invasive breast carcinoma
biomarkers.clinical_use: Larotrectinib or entrectinib for NTRK fusion-positive unresectable/metastatic solid tumors; secretory breast carcinoma is the classic breast subtype with ETV6::NTRK3 fusion

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Invasive glandular structures (ducts, tubules, cords, sheets) with variable architecture; heterogeneous
variants: invasive ductal NST (~70-80% of breast cancer)
histomorphological_subtype.grading: Nottingham combined histologic grade (Elston-Ellis): tubule formation + nuclear pleomorphism + mitotic count → grade 1-3

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Highly variable by molecular subtype — TNBC most inflamed; luminal A least; HER2+ and TNBC are the principal breast cancer settings with established immunotherapy use
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Desmoplastic stroma with cancer-associated fibroblasts; TILs increasingly quantified

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Luminal epithelial cells of terminal duct-lobular units (TDLU); intrinsic subtypes reflect distinct cell-state programs rather than simple one-to-one cell-of-origin assignments
cellular_states_and_lineage.developmental_lineage: Ectoderm (mammary bud from milk line — surface ectoderm)
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Intrinsic subtypes reflect luminal vs basal differentiation states: luminal A/B (ER+, GATA3+, FOXA1+ luminal programme), HER2-enriched, basal-like (often CK5/6+, EGFR+, basal cytokeratin programme), claudin-low (EMT-like)
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Basal-like tumors, including many TNBCs, may arise from luminal progenitors rather than mature basal/myoepithelial cells; endocrine resistance can involve luminal-to-basal lineage plasticity
